title: sutra_file_health: foundational types penalised unfairly by blast/fan-in
description:
`sutra_file_health` rates `chitta/src/error.rs` (health 43) and `envelope.rs` (55) as the *worst* files in the workspace. They aren't — they're foundational types that every other module imports. The current score weights `blast_radius_penalty: 25` and `fan_in_penalty: 11-15` for these files even though their `complexity_penalty` is 0 and `dead_symbol_penalty` is 0.

**Surfaced during:** chitta release-review spike. I had to manually annotate the SUMMARY.md to tell reviewers "ignore error.rs/envelope.rs at the top" — every consumer of file_health will hit the same friction.

## Two possible fixes

**Cheap:** add a `min_avg_cognitive` filter parameter (or a default threshold). High-blast/high-fan-in files with low cognitive complexity are *correctly* foundational and should drop out of "worst-first" output.

**Better:** decompose the score. Surface `complexity_health`, `dead_health`, `coupling_health` as separate axes. A reviewer reading "high coupling, low complexity" understands "this is a hub, not a problem"; a single-number score collapses that distinction.

I'd file the cheap fix first as a quick win; the decomposition is a bigger ask.

acceptance_criteria.text: Add filter parameter to sutra_file_health: foundational files (high fan-in + low complexity + low dead ratio) drop out of default 'worst first' ranking
OR decompose health_score into complexity_health / dead_health / coupling_health axes; tool returns all three plus an overall
Re-run on chitta workspace: error.rs and envelope.rs no longer top the list
Tool description explains foundational-type behaviour explicitly so reviewers know what they're seeing
